title: Surge Lite: compact cost/trace dashboard cutlist and acceptance decision log
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: This ticket documents the final scope reductions for the Console 'Surge Lite' launch — an intentional, reversible set of cuts to reduce telemetry and rendering cost while preserving core operator value (route-level cost awareness, basic tracing, and actionable quick-views). Goal is to lower per-session token/trace cost by ~40% in alpha while keeping the Console useful for day-1 troubleshooting. Links: PRD (Confluence) https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RED/Console+Surge+Lite+PRD, design mock (Drive) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SurgeLiteDesign, engineering proposal (GitHub) https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/182.

Scope reductions decided here (summary):
- Remove: per-route historical micro-breakdowns (minute-level charts) from alpha.
- Replace: per-route long-form cost tile with compact quick-cost summary (single-line delta + top-3 contributors) and an 'expand' CTA that opens the Cost Explorer (server-driven aggregation behind feature flag).
- Tracing: default trace sampling reduced to 1% for alpha customers; full trace detail available behind on-demand 'capture' button for canary customers.
- Dashboards: limit landing page to max 6 cards, prioritized by frequency + error impact; deferred cards moved to a collapsed 'More' pane behind a user opt-in.
- Inspectors: convert heavyweight inspector panel to a lightweight summary + link to raw logs; full inspector dock postponed to dedicated follow-up cycle.

Rationale/Trade-offs: substantial telemetry cost savings and lower render latency vs lower out-of-box visibility into minute-level anomalies. We prioritize keeping SRE/Platform troubleshooting flows intact via on-demand expansion and targeted canaries for full detail. Engineering and Design agreed this is reversible without DB remodels.

Metrics & success signals (baseline + targets):
- Baseline: median page load for Console Insights = 1.8s, telemetry ingestion cost per 1k sessions = $12. Target: page load <= 1.4s, ingestion cost per 1k sessions <= $8 (approx -33%).
- Adoption: at least 20% of alpha orgs use 'expand' CTA at least once in first 2 weeks (indicator that the compact view is discoverable).
- Regressions: no increase >5% in error creation/triage time reported by front-line PMs during alpha.

Rollback criteria: if telemetry cost reductions are <20% or critical debugging time increases >15%, pause rollout and re-enable higher-fidelity tiles for affected orgs.

Open questions (to resolve before gated rollout):
1) Backend aggregation latency SLA for the Expand CTA (ENG-39102 assigned) — target < 3s. 
2) Can we attach route tags to compact tiles without additional DB joins? (ENG follow-up required).
3) Final copy for 'More' collapsed pane and micro-CTA to surface expand behavior (Design deliverable due 2025-02-18).
acceptance_criteria: Landing page surfaces no more than 6 top-priority cards by default
Compact quick-cost summary replaces per-route long tile and shows: current delta, 3 top contributors, and a visible 'Expand' CTA
Expand CTA calls server aggregation endpoint and returns summary response within 3s for 95th percentile
Trace sampling default is set to 1% for alpha orgs; UI shows sampling state and provides on-demand full-capture for canary orgs
Cost Explorer opens from Expand CTA and shows aggregated 24h view (server-driven) without client-side minute-level charts
Inspector panel in alpha is a lightweight summary with link to raw logs; full inspector dock is not present in alpha
Gated rollout configured: 5% canary with automatic rollback trigger if page load regression > 5% or ingestion cost does not improve by at least 20%
QA checklist executed and documented: accessibility smoke, cross-browser rendering, canary instrumentation present (links to dashboards included)
Docs/Release notes prepared: short 'what changed' + how to re-enable full fidelity (internal docs + external opt-in steps)
